summary: Florence County Nicolet National Forest lookout in use in 1937; FFLA lists it as gone, and the OpenStreetMap point gives no status.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association. The OpenStreetMap point of the same name carries no status tag. No removal date found.

events.note: Junior Forester Royal M. Nettleton shot by a hunter in November while checking a seen-area map for the Long Lake lookout; he died November 28. Accounts differ on which lookout he was working on.

evidence.supports: Nettleton shot while checking a seen-area map for Long Lake Lookout from an aspen tree
evidence.quote: Nettleton was shot through the right leg late in the afternoon of November 24 while engaged in checking a 'seen area' map for Long Lake Lookout from the vantage point of an aspen tree.

evidence.supports: Nettleton of the Nicolet National Forest died November 28
evidence.quote: Junior Forester Royal M. Nettleton, 29, of the Nicolet National Forest in Wisconsin died November 28

evidence.supports: Death on Nov. 28, 1937, from a gunshot by a hunter
evidence.quote: Junior Forester Nettleton died Nov. 28, 1937, as the result of a gunshot would inflicted by Vernon Cox of Long Lake, who shot Nettleton while hunting.

evidence.supports: Second account: he was trying to get a bearing on the Jones Dam tower
evidence.quote: At the time Nettleton was shot he was up in an aspen tree endeavoring to get a bearing on the Jones Dam tower.

evidence.supports: Nicolet forest had 16 fire lookout towers in 1938
evidence.quote: The tower selected to bear Mr. Nettleton's name is the newest and most modern of the 16 fire lookout towers on the Nicolet forest.

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap point named Long Lake Lookout Tower exists
The point's tags include tower:type, with no status tag listed
The tower:type tag value is observation

corrections.proposed: No OSM status conflict; status gone per FFLA
corrections.why: The OSM node page lists its name, man_made=tower and tower:type=observation tags. It has no status tag and does not say the tower stands.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the tower as gone. The OSM point carries no status, so it does not contradict FFLA.

One February 1938 account quoted by Central US Lookouts ties Nettleton's work to Long Lake Lookout; a June 1938 Rhinelander Daily News item quoted there says he was getting a bearing on the Jones Dam tower. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Built date, staffing and site condition not found. Status rests on FFLA; the brief's osm=standing conflict is not supported by the OSM page. The two 1938 accounts disagree on which lookout Nettleton was using; the story says so. Court outcome for the shooter differs between pages (first-degree murder charge with not-guilty plea vs manslaughter acquittal); left out as outside the lookout's history. Nicolet history pages checked (npshistory chapters 3 and 7, the 1928-1976 PDF) did not show Long Lake's construction. A 1970 USGS map reference found in search was not read.
